documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Academic Senate
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10) - Campus Updates for Students
documents.summary: Provost's August 2026 message to students summarizing the revised Academic Integrity Policy S26-10. On AI it says rules vary by course, students should read syllabi and ask when unsure, and it lists campus AI-literacy and writing resources; the rest covers reporting and appeals.
documents.stance_why: Provost's student-facing summary of policy S26-10. It sets no AI rule itself and says 'Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment. Your instructors will explain what is permitted', so the decision is delegated to instructors.

units.why: The Academic Senate action is stated as the source of the policy: 'The Academic Senate has approved an updated Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10)'. This describes who adopted the policy, so P84.
units.anchor: The Academic Senate has approved an updated

units.why: The sentence says the revision 'responds to changes in teaching, learning, and technology, including the growing use of artificial intelligence', giving the purpose of the update, so an institution-level framework statement (P56).
units.anchor: responds to changes in teaching, learning, and technology, including the growing use of artificial intelligence

units.why: States that 'Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment', i.e. the decision is made per course and assignment, so P04 rather than a default stance.
units.anchor: Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment.
units.frag_start: Rules for using AI may vary

units.why: Students are told to 'read your syllabus and assignment instructions carefully' since instructors explain what is permitted; this is the student duty to learn each course's rules (P78), not the instructor duty to publish them (P09).
units.anchor: read your syllabus and assignment instructions carefully

units.why: 'If you are unsure whether you may use an AI tool... ask your instructor before submitting your work' is the ask-first rule (P10); it also covers how to acknowledge use.
units.anchor: ask your instructor before submitting your work
units.frag_start: If you are unsure whether you

units.why: The AI Literacy Essentials course for students is described as helping them 'think through the use of AI in their everyday lives and in their academic work', a student AI-literacy offering (P70).
units.anchor: helps students think through the use of AI in their everyday lives

units.why: The Career Center is said to offer 'numerous training opportunities' that help students use AI tools ethically and responsibly: training for students, so P70.
units.anchor: numerous training opportunities for students as well

units.why: Points students to the Writing Center and its 'tutoring appointments' alongside the AI Writer's Toolbox, which is human help next to AI guidance (P72).
units.anchor: SJSU Writing Center, where you can also book
units.fit_note: The Writing Center is also named as co-author of the AI Writer's Toolbox; the unit mainly points to human tutoring.

units.why: Students are told 'If you do your own work, follow your instructor's directions, and ask questions when something is unclear, you are already meeting these expectations': submitted work must be the student's own (P29).
units.anchor: If you do your own work, follow your instructor’s
units.fit_note: Also says to follow instructor directions and ask questions; the unit centers on doing one's own work.

units.why: Gives the reason for integrity rules: 'helps ensure that every student is evaluated fairly', a fairness rationale (P95) rather than a skill-building one.
units.anchor: helps ensure that every student is evaluated fairly

units.why: 'Instructors are expected to discuss the concern with you and explain any proposed academic sanction before reporting' means talk with the student before escalating (P57).
units.anchor: Instructors are expected to discuss the concern with you

units.why: 'Reports must be submitted within the policy's timeline' is a procedural reporting duty to SCED (P81).
units.anchor: Reports must be submitted within the policy’s timeline

units.why: 'You also have the right to appeal' a sanction, reviewed by the ADRRC giving 'an opportunity for you to be heard': students may respond to allegations (P64).
units.anchor: You also have the right to appeal
units.frag_end: opportunity for you to be heard.

documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Academic Senate
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10) - Campus Updates for Faculty
documents.summary: Provost's August 2026 message to faculty listing changes in S26-10. Relevant AI content: instructors decide and must communicate AI rules in syllabi, AI detection reports (Turnitin) may only be supporting evidence, plus reporting timelines, a sanctioning matrix and CFETI support.
documents.stance_why: Provost's faculty message on S26-10 says 'Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools in their courses'; no university-wide stance is set, so the decision is delegated.

units.why: The Senate action is the policy's adoption: 'The Academic Senate has approved a revised Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10)', so P84.
units.anchor: The Academic Senate has approved a revised
units.fit_note: Also thanks those who contributed to the work.

units.why: The message says generative AI and detector limits 'raise new questions' and the policy needed 'clearer expectations and more consistent procedures'; this explains why the policy changed, P56.
units.anchor: the rapid growth of generative artificial intelligence
units.frag_start: Changes in teaching, learning, and technology
units.fit_note: Also states doubts about the efficacy of AI detection technologies.

units.why: Gives a fairness and confidence rationale: integrity 'helps ensure that students are evaluated fairly' and that employers can trust an SJSU degree: P95.
units.anchor: helps ensure that students are evaluated fairly

units.why: 'You must report the matter to Student Conduct and Ethical Development' plus the rule that a sanction 'may not be imposed without submitting' the reporting form is a mandatory reporting procedure (P81).
units.anchor: an academic sanction may not be imposed without submitting
units.frag_start: If you determine that an academic

units.why: The reason given, that consistent reporting 'allows the university to identify repeat violations, provide appropriate support', explains the reporting rule; closest type is P81.
units.anchor: Consistent reporting allows the university to identify repeat violations
units.fit_note: This is a rationale for reporting rather than a procedural step.

units.why: 'You are expected to communicate and confer with the student within 10 working days' means talk with the student first and within a deadline: P57.
units.anchor: communicate and confer with the student within 10 working days
units.frag_start: As a faculty member, you are
units.frag_end: release of the grade for the assessment.
units.fit_note: Adds a 10-working-day deadline and a no-later-than grade-release limit.

units.why: The report 'must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident' is a procedural deadline in the formal reporting process, P81.
units.anchor: must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident

units.why: 'Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools in their courses' places the AI decision with each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools

units.why: 'Make sure to communicate those expectations clearly in your syllabi and assignment instructions' obliges instructors to state AI expectations, P09; includes acknowledgement requirements.
units.anchor: communicate those expectations clearly in your syllabi and assignment instructions

units.why: 'you may want to use SJSU's AI Policy Builder' is a tool offered to help instructors write their course AI policy: faculty support (P63).
units.anchor: To craft an AI policy for your course, you may want to use
units.fit_note: A tool for drafting course AI policy rather than a workshop or consultation.

units.why: 'Faculty may only use detection services approved by the university. At SJSU, you have access to Turnitin' limits detection to approved tools (P40, detector use).
units.anchor: Faculty may only use detection services approved by the university.
units.fit_note: The rule limits detection to university-approved services rather than telling faculty to use similarity checks.

units.why: Detection tools 'must, however, be approached with great caution as they have become less effective over time' with false positives; the message warns against reliance on detectors (P39).
units.anchor: must, however, be approached with great caution
units.frag_start: These detection tools and their findings

units.why: AI detection reports 'cannot serve as the sole basis for imposing an academic sanction' sets a rule on evidence standards (P69).
units.anchor: They cannot serve as the sole basis for imposing an academic

units.why: Lists what 'Other evidence may include': a significant change from the student's previous work or inconsistency with class materials, i.e. kinds of evidence to weigh (P69).
units.anchor: a significant or noteworthy change from the student’s previous work

units.why: The policy 'introduces a sanctioning matrix with recommended sanctions based on the nature and severity of a violation', a stated penalty guide (P37).
units.anchor: introduces a sanctioning matrix
units.frag_end: nature and severity of a violation.
units.fit_note: Recommended sanctions by severity, not specific AI penalties; it is a matrix, not stated penalties.

units.why: 'The matrix is a guide, not a substitute for faculty judgment' says the sanctions are advisory and leave room for case circumstances; nearest type P37.
units.anchor: The matrix is a guide, not a substitute for faculty judgment.
units.fit_note: Says the penalties are discretionary rather than stating penalties.

units.why: CFETI 'can provide you with relevant AI Pedagogical Resources' and offers consultations: faculty support in learning AI (P63).
units.anchor: The Center offers in-person and Zoom consultations for individual faculty members

units.why: CFETI consultations also help faculty 'better understand the effectiveness, limits, and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin', faculty support about detectors (P63).
units.anchor: better understand the effectiveness, limits, and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin

units.why: Turnitin Clarity workshop on a tool that 'reveal[s] drafting history and guide[s] responsible AI usage' is faculty training; nearest type P63 though the tool itself is process evidence.
units.anchor: Turnitin Clarity–a tool that focuses on the student’s writing process
units.fit_note: Also describes a pilot of a drafting-history tool (process evidence, P40).

units.why: 'please review the revised policy, update your course materials as needed' tells faculty to keep up with the policy and adjust materials (P102).
units.anchor: please review the revised policy, update your course materials as needed

units.why: 'Additional resources and training on S26-10 and Academic Integrity, will become available' announces faculty training to come (P63).
units.anchor: Additional resources and training on S26-10 and Academic Integrity

documents.title: Developing a Generative AI Syllabus Policy
documents.summary: Library and CFETI guide for faculty on writing a generative-AI syllabus policy under S26-10. It requires instructors to state their AI policy and links to the AI Policy Builder, pedagogical resources and a student AI disclosure resource (SAID).
documents.stance_why: The library guide says 'Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI depending on the course and assignment', so it sets no stance and delegates to instructors, with three approaches as tiers.

units.why: States that S26-10 'requires instructors to communicate their course policy regarding the use of artificial intelligence... in the syllabus': a syllabus-statement mandate (P09).
units.anchor: requires instructors to communicate their course policy regarding the use of artificial intelligence

units.why: 'Faculty should clearly explain whether and how generative AI may be used in their course, including expectations for acknowledgment or citation': directs content of the syllabus statement; P09 is the nearest.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly explain whether and how generative AI may be used
units.fit_note: Also asks instructors to say whether and how acknowledgment or citation is expected.

units.why: The Policy Builder lets faculty create a statement using 'approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit generative AI use', named categories of approach (P05).
units.anchor: approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit generative AI use
units.fit_note: Three approaches are named, but no levels are defined within the text.

units.why: The pedagogical resources are 'guidance for incorporating, limiting, or addressing AI use in teaching', faculty support in learning AI (P63).
units.anchor: Guidance for incorporating, limiting, or addressing AI use in teaching and coursework.

units.why: SAID is 'A resource faculty can use to help students document how they used AI in their coursework', supporting student documentation of AI use (P26).
units.anchor: help students document how they used AI in their coursework
units.fit_note: A resource for documenting use, not a requirement to keep transcripts or reflections.

units.why: 'Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI depending on the course and assignment' puts the rule with instructors, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI

units.why: 'communicate expectations clearly in both the syllabus and assignment instructions' extends the communication duty to assignment level; P09.
units.anchor: communicate expectations clearly in both the syllabus and assignment instructions
units.fit_note: Names both the syllabus and the assignment instructions as places.

documents.title: Academic Integrity (School of Information)
documents.date_or_term: undated; cites the ChatGPT Sep 14 2023 version
documents.summary: School of Information academic integrity page with a short AI-Assisted Software policy (v1, Sept 2023): AI use must be cited in APA format, failure to cite violates F15-7, and students unsure should confer with the instructor. The rest of the page covers general plagiarism procedures.
documents.stance_why: AI use is allowed provided it is cited: 'The use of ChatGPT and any other AI-assisted software must be cited as a reference source'. No ban is stated, so permit with a citation condition.

units.why: States 'must be cited as a reference source', a disclosure-with-submission rule for any AI-assisted software (P24).
units.anchor: must be cited as a reference source
units.frag_start: The use of ChatGPT and any
units.frag_end: where ideas and sentences are used from other sources.

units.why: 'Failure to cite the use of any AI-assisted software constitutes a violation of SJSU policy F15-7': nondisclosure is itself the violation (P28), chosen over P36 because the offense is specifically failure to cite.
units.anchor: Failure to cite the use of any AI-assisted software constitutes a violation

units.why: 'This policy is not exhaustive. If students are uncertain... it is their responsibility to confer with the instructor': ask the instructor when unsure (P10).
units.anchor: it is their responsibility to confer with the instructor of that particular course
units.frag_start: If students are uncertain as to

units.why: Instructs 'you are to cite the use of AI-Assisted software as follows' with in-text (OpenAI, 2023) and reference naming the tool and version: citation details (P25).
units.anchor: In the APA editorial style, you are to cite the use of AI-Assisted software
units.fit_note: Specifies the tool, year and version date but not the prompt or output.

units.why: Records that the policy was 'v1 adopted on September 14, 2023', saying when the school policy was adopted (P84).
units.anchor: v1 adopted on September 14, 2023

notes: Coder A. Policy text S26-10 itself was not in the saved text, only provost summaries. The School of Information page's general plagiarism sanctions and Turnitin similarity-check lines are not AI-specific and were not coded. Course layer deferred in collect.
